proposals.title: Spatial Trajectory Mapping with Neighborhood Constraints
proposals.summary: This analysis would focus on tracing developmental or disease-related trajectories by combining gene expression profiles with physical proximity constraints. The method involves constructing a spatial graph where nodes represent spots or cells and edges reflect neighboring relationships based on distance. Trajectory paths are then inferred using graph-based diffusion or similar algorithms, with emphasis on ensuring that the signal is localized and corresponds with known anatomical landmarks. The approach can be validated using time course data or independent imaging techniques.

proposals.title: Integrated Ligand-Receptor Co-occurrence Filtering
proposals.summary: This analysis will enhance the identification of cell-cell communication events by integrating ligand-receptor expression data with spatial distance filters. The strategy involves correlating known ligand-receptor pairs across spatially adjacent locations and applying thresholds based on physical separation. By combining molecular co-expression with spatial constraints, the method reduces false positives inherent in expression-only analyses and provides interpretable insights into paracrine and juxtacrine signaling processes.

proposals.title: Noise Reduction via Multimodal Data Integration
proposals.summary: A common challenge with spatial transcriptomics is the sparsity of data and technical noise. This analysis proposes an integrative approach that combines gene expression with imaging and coordinate data to enhance signal detection. The method employs adaptive filtering or smoothing techniques that respect the spatial architecture of the sample while aligning with tissue morphology. The integration allows the identification of robust expression patterns by leveraging complementary information from both modalities.

proposals.title: Spatial Cell-Type Deconvolution Anchored by Tissue Morphology
proposals.summary: This analysis is designed to deconvolve mixed cellular signals in spots that may contain diverse cell types. By integrating morphological features with gene expression profiles, spatial deconvolution algorithms can assign probabilities of cell-type identity within each spot. This approach leverages the inherent spatial organization of tissues, ensuring that inferred cell types follow known anatomical distributions. The outcome will provide refined maps of tissue composition even in regions of overlapping cell types.

proposals.title: 3D Tissue Reconstruction Through Serial Section Registration
proposals.summary: Since many spatial transcriptomics assays capture sections rather than an entire 3D structure, this analysis focuses on computationally reconstructing three-dimensional spatial expression landscapes. It combines serial section imaging and registration methods with expression data from each section to create a coherent 3D map. The process incorporates spatial and morphological cues to align sections, enabling the study of tissue architecture and developmental trajectories across volumes.

proposals.title: Spatial Dynamics of Gene Expression in Injury and Repair
proposals.summary: To study tissue injury and regeneration, this analysis will map the spatial dynamics of gene expression in relation to damage sites. It will involve segmenting areas of injury using imaging data, then correlating molecular changes to the distance from the injury epicenter. By applying spatial smoothing and trajectory analysis, the method identifies gradients of repair or inflammatory responses, thereby revealing the coordinated nature of tissue healing.

proposals.title: Validation of Cell-Cell Communication using Known Anatomical Landmarks
proposals.summary: This proposal aims to refine predictions of cell-cell communication by cross-validating co-occurring ligand-receptor pairs with established anatomical structures. The analysis first identifies putative interacting cells based on expression data and spatial proximity, then uses reference anatomical maps or immunohistochemistry data to confirm biologically plausible interactions. This multi-layered approach helps in filtering out spurious signals that arise solely from expression correlations.

proposals.title: Multi-Scale Neighborhood Profiling for Rare Cell States
proposals.summary: Rare cellular states can be challenging to identify in noisy spatial transcriptomics datasets. This analysis employs multi-scale neighborhood profiling, where local expression averages and global spatial patterns are integrated to highlight subtle transitions. By considering varying spatial definitions of neighborhoods and introducing adaptive window sizes, the method increases sensitivity to rare states while maintaining robustness against outlier signals.

proposals.title: Morphology-Assisted Inference of Gene Expression Trajectories
proposals.summary: This approach integrates tissue morphology, such as cell shape and tissue boundaries, with spatial gene expression to infer developmental or pathological trajectories. Detailed segmentation of tissue regions, in combination with spatially resolved expression profiles, allows for the tracking of cell state changes along morphological gradients. The method enhances trajectory inference by grounded spatial context, making the biological interpretation more intuitive and verifiable with histological images.

proposals.title: Temporal Validation of Spatial Patterns through Independent Imaging Data
proposals.summary: Recognizing that spatial transcriptomics snapshots may be influenced by technical and biological variability, this analysis incorporates independent temporal imaging data. The approach involves mapping spatial expression patterns from a series of time points and cross-validating these patterns with live-imaging or sequential histological data. By aligning transcriptomics data with independent imaging modalities, this analysis supports robust inference of spatial-temporal dynamics in tissue development or disease progression.
